clue.text: Beaten by a small creature like little Edward!

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep, a small creature
as means like, in the manner of
Ted is the pet form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Someone has been knocked about by a tiny animal, just as young Teddy was.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambaste someone is to thrash or attack them, so the past form means thrashed.

clue.text: Innocent little children finding revolutionary leader abrasive

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born leader of the Cuban revolution
a thing that is abrasive rubs or chafes, so rubs stands for being abrasive

explanation.surface: Small innocent children discover that the leader of a revolution is grating company.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubs are winged child angels, so the word is used for sweet, innocent-looking youngsters.

clue.text: Article with hints about poetry in places like Australia

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hints go round the poetry

parts.note: tips are hints or pieces of advice
an ode is a lyric poem, a piece of poetry

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece offers advice on verse written in faraway lands down under.
explanation.definitionFit: The antipodes are places on the opposite side of the globe, a British term for Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: At the opera, see female smile widely

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a hen is a female bird
to grin is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: In the opera house, a woman spots another woman beaming broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the' is a link phrase leading to the definition, which is just 'opera'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lohengrin is Wagner's romantic opera about the swan knight.

clue.text: Tree a boy with nothing on is climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the run of letters goes backwards

parts.note: Ned is a boy's name
nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A naked lad is shinning up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is climbing' turns NED with NIL on it, giving LIN then DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The linden is the lime tree, genus Tilia.

clue.text: With this optical device, damaged pie on range

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so the letters of pie are rearranged

parts.note: scope means range or extent

explanation.surface: Peering through some instrument, you can see a spoilt pie sitting on the cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges PIE to EPI; 'range' looks like a kitchen stove but means scope.
explanation.definitionFit: An episcope is a projector that throws an image of an opaque object such as a page onto a screen.

clue.text: Very small bug — non-specific — in the country

parts.note: a germ is a microbe, a tiny bug
any means no particular one

explanation.surface: Some unidentified microbe is going round in the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany is a nation of central Europe.

clue.text: Bug eating apple core? Look into this!

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the bug goes round the other piece

parts.note: a bug is an insect

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter, here of apple

explanation.surface: A grub has burrowed into the middle of a piece of fruit, so have a look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The core of APPLE is its middle letter P, which goes inside INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something is to examine it closely.

clue.text: In Ghana for example greeting, embracing social worker

parts.note: as can mean for example, such as

indicators.note: embracing means holding round, so the greeting goes round the worker

parts.note: hi is a greeting
an ant is a social insect, and a worker ant is the typical one

explanation.surface: A Ghanaian welcome is given with a hug to a welfare officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' looks like a welfare officer but is an ANT, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashanti is a region of Ghana, once a powerful kingdom of the Akan people.

clue.text: Come back into line, in mid-flight, then stray away

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the middle of flight goes into the other word

parts.note: soldiers dress ranks when they straighten up into line

indicators.note: mid- picks the centre of a word, here flight

explanation.surface: A bird or plane returns to formation partway through a journey and then wanders off.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters of FLIGHT are IG, which go into DRESS; 'dress' is the parade-ground order to line up.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to wander from the main subject.

clue.text: Holly may be put underneath, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: buried means put under the ground

explanation.surface: Holly might be dug in under the soil, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly is a shrub that bears bright red fruit, so it can be described as bearing berries.

clue.text: Returned from a diet experiment — with this appearance?

indicators.note: an experiment tries things out in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: came back means returned, so returned gives came

explanation.surface: Someone back from trying out a new diet looks like this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'experiment' rearranges CAME plus A DIET; 'Returned' gives CAME, not a backwards signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin, the gaunt look an extreme diet might leave.

clue.text: Italian sheepdog seen to injure a girl

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or injure
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A dog from Italy is spotted harming a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The maremma is a large white Italian guard and herding dog.

clue.text: Mess of bean soup served to order

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of the soup are muddled

explanation.surface: A muddle of beany soup is dished up on request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served to' links the anagram to the definition: a summons is something served.
explanation.definitionFit: A subpoena is a writ ordering someone to appear in court.

clue.text: Eye pot — source of liquor

annotationWithheld.why: 'Eye pot — source of liquor' as held: EYE POT rearranged gives the answer but no word signals an anagram, so the clue looks cut short in the OCR.

clue.text: Diesels we deployed in the plant

indicators.note: deployed means spread out in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Diesel engines we have put to use at the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is an alpine flower with woolly white bracts.

clue.text: Being over sixteen and Anglican

indicators.note: over can mean upset or knocked over, so the letters of sixteen are rearranged

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: Someone is past sixteen and a member of the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Being and existence both mean the state of living or being real.

clue.text: Having key to rented building, moved in

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: building means constructing something new, so the letters of rented are reassembled

explanation.surface: With a key to a leased block, someone has taken up residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Entered means went into or came inside.

clue.text: Unfamiliar figure could make men cower

indicators.note: could make means could be turned into, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A stranger might cause the chaps to cringe.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer is someone who has just arrived and is not yet known.

clue.text: Relax your guard when at one point, weapon is withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the weapon is read backwards

parts.note: a sword is a weapon
E, east, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Ease off when, at one moment, the blade is sheathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' turns SWORD into DROWS; 'one point' is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To drowse is to doze, letting your vigilance slip.

clue.text: An improving suggestion for artist --- -heartless rogue — turn out for church!

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is removed, leaving the first and last letters of rogue
turn means rotate or shift about, so the letters of out are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to a painter: a cruel scoundrel should show up for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves RE from ROGUE; 'turn' rearranges OUT to TOU.
explanation.definitionFit: A retouch is a small touch-up that improves a painting or photograph.

clue.text: Reaches the conclusion it makes one nervous

definitions.meaning: brings things to an end, finishes

explanation.surface: Coming to the end is what makes a person anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind up is to bring to a close; to wind someone up is also to make them tense or agitated.

clue.text: Relatives with money entertaining us

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the money holds the other word inside

parts.note: coins are money

explanation.surface: Family members with cash are treating us.
explanation.definitionFit: Cousins are the children of your aunts and uncles.

clue.text: Post plenty of swim-suits for the ladies

parts.note: mail is post, letters
lots means plenty

explanation.surface: Send a great many ladies' bathing costumes by mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A maillot is a one-piece women's swimming costume.

clue.text: It is in A flat, on a lute, though not keeping to that one key

definitions.text: not keeping to that one key

indicators.note: is in means is contained within, so the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: A tune in A flat played on a lute, though it wanders off the key.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across flAT ON A Lute.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music has no tonal centre, so it does not stay in a single key.

clue.text: Cat has grabbed her head — having first destroyed nest with egg in it

definitions.text: Cat has grabbed her head — having first destroyed nest with egg in it

indicators.note: having first means this piece comes before the other
in it means placed inside, so the egg goes within the wrecked nest
destroyed means wrecked, so the letters of nest are scattered

parts.note: an egg is round, like the letter O

indicators.note: has grabbed means holds, so the cat goes round the letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: head means the first letter of her

explanation.surface: A cat seizes a bird by the head after wrecking its nest with an egg in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges NEST round the O, making STONE; 'has grabbed' puts H, the head of 'her', into CAT for CHAT. The whole clue describes a cat catching this small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small European bird, which a cat might catch after raiding its nest.

clue.text: Ring leading engineer about lines to keep an eye upon

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so the ring goes at the front

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
lines of poetry are verse
E is an abbreviation for engineer

explanation.surface: The chief of a gang leads an engineer around the railway tracks to watch over him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word meaning concerning here.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise, watching over work or people.

clue.text: Express anger about student thus becoming excessively offensive

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anger goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to fume is to show rage
L, the learner plate, stands for a student
so means thus

explanation.surface: Someone rages at a pupil and so becomes overly rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulsome means excessively flattering, in the old sense cloying or offensive to good taste.

clue.text: Poison scare in cooking

indicators.note: cooking means being cooked up, so the letters of the fodder are reworked

explanation.surface: A poison alarm breaks out in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the anagram fodder with SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a toxic chemical element, the classic poisoner's choice.

clue.text: Fellow with a Rolls-Royce — a learner-in the thicket

parts.note: a chap is a fellow, a man
L, as on a learner plate, stands for a learner

explanation.surface: A man with a luxury car and a learner driver end up in the bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaparral is dense scrub or thicket of the American Southwest.
